title: Soft Tofu Stew
summary: Fry the chilli flakes in oil to draw out chilli oil, then build the stew on it. The colour and the flavour both change.
intro:
The red broth of sundubu-jjigae does not come from stirring chilli flakes into water. They have to be fried in oil first, so the pigment dissolves into the fat and the broth turns a clear red.

Chilli flakes burn in 30 seconds, though. Keep the heat low and do not look away.
steps: Soak the clams in salted water for 30 minutes to purge the sand, then scrub them clean.
Heat the oil in an earthenware pot (ttukbaegi) over low heat, add the chilli flakes and stir for 20-30 seconds only, to draw out the chilli oil. If it smokes, it has already burnt.
Add the pork and minced garlic and fry over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add the onion and zucchini and fry for 1 minute more.
Pour in the broth and bring to the boil over high heat. Once it boils, add the clams.
When the clams open, spoon in the silken tofu in large pieces. Do not stir; leave it as it is.
Season with the soup soy sauce and salted shrimp and simmer for 3 minutes more.
Lay the spring onion, cut on the diagonal, on top and crack the egg into the middle. Turn off the heat after 30 seconds.
tips: Prawns or squid work in place of the clams, and you can leave the seafood out and use only pork. In that case, increase the salted shrimp a little.
Silken tofu breaks up the moment you stir it. Just keep it submerged in the broth and let it simmer as it is.
If you do not have a ttukbaegi, use a small pot, but move the stew into a serving bowl as soon as it is done.
